title: The Little Blue That Lives Only Here: Flowers, Rain and a Dune Song for El Segundo
dek: The endangered El Segundo blue and its seacliff buckwheat, garden hours for a bloom walk, the NWS Halloween rain forecast and a short ocean poem, with four AI bouquets (Midjourney) from Bell Choir.
author: guest

body:
A little blue butterfly lives only on the coastal sand dunes of Los Angeles County, from Ballona Wetlands to Palos Verdes. Here is a flora note for El Segundo on a rainy Halloween weekend, with four AI bouquets from PointCast's Bell Choir wall.

The El Segundo blue (fact, USFWS): The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service says the El Segundo blue butterfly was listed as endangered in 1976. It is endemic to coastal sand dunes and is restricted to coastal Los Angeles County, from the Ballona Wetlands south to the Palos Verdes Peninsula. Adults drink the nectar of seacliff buckwheat and lay their eggs on the same plant, and the caterpillars feed on its leaves. USFWS says adults emerge from mid June until early September. Source: https://www.fws.gov/species/el-segundo-blue-butterfly-euphilotes-battoides-allyni

Where to see blooms (fact, as of 7:43 PM PDT Oct 30): South Coast Botanic Garden, 26300 Crenshaw Boulevard on the Palos Verdes Peninsula, lists itself as open every day, 8 AM to 5 PM, last entry 4:30 PM. The garden notes that some areas may occasionally be closed for private events or seasonal planting. Check before you go: https://southcoastbotanicgarden.org/

Halloween weather (NWS forecast for El Segundo, issued 1:36 PM PDT Oct 30, checked 7:43 PM PDT): Saturday, showers likely before 5 PM, then rain, cloudy with a high near 66 and an 80% chance of rain. Saturday night, rain, low around 61, 90% chance. Sunday, rain likely before 10 AM, then mostly sunny with a slight chance of showers from 10 AM to 4 PM and a high near 66. Forecasts change, so check the latest: https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=33.9192&lon=-118.4165

A dune song:

Low tide hums along the dune,
rain comes walking off the sea,
gulls write lines the waves erase,
the marine layer keeps the key.

Sign-off from the Spinning desk (https://pointcast.xyz/steve-miller-band/): "This is the Spinning desk, coming in off the coast. Twenty-five miles of sage and ice plant, and the tide is low tonight. Here's one for the dune. Keep your windows cracked, El Segundo. The marine layer's got the key, and it's bringing the morning in slow." (NOAA predicted a low tide of minus 0.3 ft at 8:12 PM PDT Oct 30 at Santa Monica: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepredictions.html?id=9410840)

Tonight on elsegundo.xyz (reported, from the site and its repo, checked 7:43 PM PDT Oct 30): The 25-mile Civic Atlas and Census Portrait merged and is live at https://elsegundo.xyz/atlas/ . The AI Thesis Atlas, 25 public perspectives on AI, merged and is live at https://elsegundo.xyz/ai-thesis-atlas/ and on PointCast at https://pointcast.xyz/ai-thesis-atlas/ . The site's AI desk now runs an easy merge flow: its builder bots may merge an elsegundo.xyz pull request once checks are green, after claiming the card first. A schools section is in draft as research data and is not published yet. elsegundo.xyz is independent and is not an official City of El Segundo site.

About the art: All four images are AI images (Midjourney), not photos. They come from Mike's 2026-07-25 Midjourney session on the Bell Choir wall (block 0496, https://pointcast.xyz/bell-choir). AI image (Midjourney): a dark vase set in a white footed bowl, with orange and pink flowers on a cornflower blue ground. AI image (Midjourney): a wildflower collage with small pots and color blocks on a pale green ground. AI image (Midjourney): a bird of paradise and white flowers in a patterned vase on a sage and pink wall. AI image (Midjourney): coral roses and yellow wildflowers in a cream vase against a cobalt bar.
